description:
Fix clinical trial sample sizes for unequal allocation

With --allocation set to anything other than 1, the clinical-trial-protocol
skill's sample_size_calculator.py returned the wrong group sizes. It asked
for too few participants at ratios above about 1.6:1 for continuous
endpoints and above 1:1 for binary endpoints, and for too many at ratios
below 1:1 (at 1:2, about six times too many for continuous endpoints and
about twice too many for binary ones). The default 1:1 group sizes were
correct, and the commands written in the skill never pass --allocation.

Examples, at two-sided alpha 0.05 and 80% target power, before dropout:

  Difference of 1 standard deviation, 2:1
    before: 18 + 9 = 27, fewer than the 32 needed at 1:1; real power 65%
    now:    24 + 12 = 36; real power 78% (see the second known limit)
  Response rate 60% vs 75%, 2:1
    before: 110 + 55 = 165; real power 51%
    now:    224 + 112 = 336; real power 80%

What changes:

- Both endpoint types now size the control group with the standard
  formula, round it up, and multiply by the ratio to get the treatment
  group. The main result and both sensitivity rows use the same code.
- At 1:1 the only number that moves is the binary "effect size reduced
  by 10%" sensitivity row, which now pools the rates using the reduced
  treatment rate (60% vs 75%: 378 becomes 380).
- One-line errors replace crashes or meaningless results when the
  allocation ratio is not a positive number, the effect size is zero,
  the standard deviation is not positive, or p1 equals p2.
- --design accepts "noninferiority" as well as "non-inferiority".
- The skill's instructions now say not to run the calculator for
  non-inferiority designs: tell the user why, and use enrollment numbers
  from similar trials with the existing disclaimer instead. That is
  where the written instructions already led, because their commands
  passed "noninferiority" and the script rejected it. They also say to
  tell the user when the protocol's study design section and the user's
  answer name different designs.
- When the calculation fails or is skipped, the instructions now also
  say not to use a result file left from an earlier run, and to report
  the calculation as not performed.
- SKILL.md no longer calls the calculator "validated" or "accurate".
  Unit tests are added next to it, with expected values from published
  examples and from the standard formulas. Run them with:
  python3 clinical-trial-protocol-skill/scripts/test_sample_size_calculator.py

Known limits, not changed here:

- Non-inferiority has no margin option. The script sizes the trial to
  detect --effect-size (or p2 - p1), with alpha used as one-sided.
- Continuous sizes use the normal approximation, so they come out one or
  two participants per group short of an exact t-test calculation (at a
  1 SD difference, 16 per group gives 78% power, not 80%; at 2 SD, 4 per
  group gives 66%).
- For continuous endpoints, a ratio and its inverse (3:1 and 1:3) can
  differ by a few participants, because the control group is the one
  rounded first.
- --alpha, --power and --dropout are not range-checked. Values of 0, 1
  or outside 0 to 1 can stop with a Python traceback or give meaningless
  numbers; a dropout rate above 1, such as 15 for 15%, gives negative
  enrollment numbers.
- The v1.1.0 and v1.1.1 tags contain the old script.

command/providers mirror: Refactor to use `views` (#39466)

This change:

* Makes the `arguments` package control the selected view type for `providers mirror`
* Implements a human view for the `providers mirror` command
* Makes the `providers mirror` command use views to prepare and print output

There are a number of places that can be improved here in future. Mainly, there is overlap between logging events here and in `init`. When (SRO-style) JSON output is added we need to think about shared event types across commands here, and reconcile that with how `providers mirror` logs different data to `init`.

Here's a copy of my [comment on this change's PR](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/39466#discussion_r4403011817):

>There are some provider installation events that are common to all commands that download providers, e.g. acknowledging use of built-in provider, downloading a latest version, reporting that a provider version was successfully downloaded, etc.
>
>The methods logging these events are: init, state migrate, providers mirror, providers lock.
>
>Currently the data used to log those events is different between these commands, e.g. providers mirror can download for multiple platforms and so includes platform data in messages. The init command doesn't log platform data as it's kinda implied that it's only downloading for the current platform in use.
>
>In future I'd love to have interfaces that are re-used by all these commands. The methods would need to be able to accept all possible bits of input data describing an event type. This becomes more important if/when JSON output is added to the providers subcommands, as the schema of the JSON object would need to be equally applicable across all commands logging these events. The human-readable output can continue to not use certain bits of data when creating messages, but the JSON output would need to be richer.

description:
Push table_name/table_oid filters into duckdb_tables(), duckdb_views() and duckdb_columns() (#27930)

## Summary

#27291 taught `duckdb_tables()` and `duckdb_views()` to accept filters
on their catalog and schema identity columns, so a query that names a
schema no longer lists the tables of every schema in every attached
catalog. That work stopped one level short of the table itself: a
predicate on `table_name` is still applied above the scan, so a query
that asks about one table still lists every table in the schema. It also
never reached `duckdb_columns()`, which has no pushdown at all today and
enumerates every schema of every attached catalog in `Init` before any
filtering happens. For a remote catalog such as the Glue extension,
`SELECT column_name, data_type FROM duckdb_columns() WHERE schema_name =
's' AND table_name = 't'` therefore costs one database-listing call plus
one `GetTables` call per database in the account, to return the columns
of a single table.

This PR extends the pushdown to the entry identity columns
(`table_name`/`table_oid`, and `view_name`/`view_oid` for
`duckdb_views()`), gives the schema entry a hook to serve those filters
with its own lookup strategy, and wires `duckdb_columns()` into the
scanner at both levels so it finally benefits from the schema-level
pruning from #27291 as well as the new table-level pruning.

## High Level Impact

Before: `duckdb_columns()` lists every schema of every attached catalog
and then every table of every schema, and only then applies the `WHERE`
clause. `duckdb_tables()` and `duckdb_views()` prune catalogs and
schemas but still list every table of each surviving schema before a
`table_name` predicate is applied.

After, for a predicate on `table_name`/`table_oid` (or
`view_name`/`view_oid`), the filter travels with the scan into `Init`,
where it is handed to each surviving schema when its entries are
requested. The default behaviour is to list the schema's entries and
keep the ones the filter accepts, so for DuckDB's own catalog nothing
changes except where the filtering happens. A catalog may override the
new `SchemaCatalogEntry::Scan(ClientContext &, SchemaScanInfo &)` to
avoid the listing, for example a remote catalog answering a `table_name`
equality with a single lookup instead of listing the schema. The scanner
re-checks every entry the schema hands back, so an override can only
lose the saving, never change the result.

`duckdb_columns()` additionally gains the schema-level pruning from
#27291, which it did not have before.

## Changes

**Entry-level filters in `SystemCatalogScanner`** --
`SystemCatalogScannerData` records the positions of the function's entry
name and oid columns alongside the four catalog/schema columns. Because
the entry column is not named uniformly across the system functions
(`table_name` in `duckdb_tables()`, `view_name` in `duckdb_views()`),
and because a column called `table_name` is not always the scanned
entry's own name (in `duckdb_indexes()` it is the parent table), the
function passes the two column names to `CreateBindData` rather than the
helper guessing them. `CreateBindData` now also checks the column's
type, so a column that merely shares an identity column's name is not
treated as pushable. The filter-bucketing loop that `GetSchemas` already
performed is extracted into `CollectFilters`, and a new `GetEntries`
helper prunes the schemas exactly as before and then collects each
surviving schema's entries through the new hook, re-checking every
returned entry with `EntryScanFilters::Accepts`. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`
reports `Entries Scanned` next to the existing `Catalogs Scanned` /
`Schemas Scanned`.

**`SchemaCatalogEntry::Scan(ClientContext &, SchemaScanInfo &)`** -- a
new `Scan` overload alongside the existing three. `SchemaScanInfo`
bundles the entry type, the per-entry callback and an optional
`EntryScanFilters`, so later additions to a schema scan extend the
struct rather than the vtable. The default forwards to the existing
`Scan` and invokes the callback only for entries the filter accepts.
`EntryScanFilters` is the entry-level twin of `SchemaScanFilters`: two
optional filters evaluated with
`ExpressionFilter::EvaluateWithConstant`, with private members and
accessors (`SchemaScanFilters` gets the same treatment). An override may
invoke the callback on a superset of the matches; the scanner re-checks
each entry in the callback it passes, so catalog-specific knowledge such
as case semantics stays in the catalog.

**Function conversions** -- `duckdb_tables()` and `duckdb_views()` name
their entry columns in `CreateBindData` and replace the per-schema
`Scan` loop in `Init` with one `GetEntries` call. `duckdb_columns()` is
converted for the first time: it gets a bind function, the `GetEntries`
call, `RegisterPushdown` and the metrics callback, so filters on all six
identity columns now reach the scanner.

**Tests** -- a new sqllogictest `system_catalog_entry_pushdown.test`
covers the three functions with their own fixture: plan shape (the
pushed predicate appears under `Filters:` on the scan, non-identity
predicates stay above it), row-level results for `table_name`,
`table_oid`, `view_name` and combined schema-plus-table predicates,
`lower()`, `IN` and `LIKE` shapes, the `WITH ORDINALITY` path, and the
`Entries Scanned` counters. In `system_catalog_scanner.test`, the one
existing assertion that a `table_name` predicate is not pushed is
updated to expect that it is, with `comment = 'x'` taking its place as
the non-identity example.

## Results

Measured against an AWS Glue Data Catalog in `us-east-1` with **80
databases** (Glue databases are DuckDB schemas). The statement timed is
the one from the summary, against the 31-column table
`tpcds_hive_1gb.call_center`:

```sql
SELECT column_name, data_type FROM duckdb_columns()
WHERE schema_name = 'tpcds_hive_1gb' AND table_name = 'call_center'
```

Baseline is the branch point; both variants use the same build of the
Glue extension. 5 iterations per variant, interleaved, each a fresh
process (`LOAD`, secret, `ATTACH`, then the statement). Glue calls are
counted from DuckDB's HTTP log and were identical on every iteration.

| Variant | Glue calls for the statement | Latency, median (min..max) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | **81** -- `GetDatabases` x1, `GetTables` x80 | **10.76 s**
(9.68 .. 11.06 s) |
| This PR | 2 -- `GetDatabase` x1, `GetTables` x1 | 0.66 s (0.61 .. 0.70
s) |

Both return the same 31 rows on every iteration. About 440 ms of each
figure is `LOAD`/secret/`ATTACH`, which is the same in both variants and
makes no catalog calls; the rest is the statement. The baseline's 80
`GetTables` calls are the per-database listings `duckdb_columns()`
issued because no filter reached it. With this PR the pushed
`schema_name` filter is answered by the extension with one
`GetDatabase`, and the pushed `table_name` filter is applied to the
single `GetTables` listing of the target database. That remaining
`GetTables` is what a Glue-side `Scan` override can turn into a single
`GetTable`, which is the follow-up in the extension.

description:
Fix autocomplete dropping text after the cursor (#28114)

## Summary

`describe from 'ta';` completes the tied file names to their
longest common prefix but loses the `';` that follows the cursor. Typing
the rest of the name afterwards then leaves `describe from
'table_two.parquet` without the closing quote and semicolon, so the
statement never terminates.

Fixes #27985.

## Root cause

In `Linenoise::CompleteLine`, when several completions tie, the line is
completed to their longest common prefix. Applying the prefix rewrote
the whole buffer from the completion (which covers only the text before
the cursor), so any text after the cursor was dropped. Completions
already carry the text after the cursor, which is why fully accepting a
suggestion restores the trailing `';`, but the intermediate prefix step
did not.

## Change

When applying the common prefix, append the text that followed the
cursor, minus any part already contained in the prefix. The cursor is
left after the applied prefix so further typing lands before the
preserved suffix.

## Tests

Added a pty-based regression test in
`tools/shell/tests/test_autocomplete.py` that reproduces the issue
steps: it types `describe from 'ta|';`, presses tab once, finishes the
name without tabbing again, and checks the saved history for the
semicolon-terminated statement. The test is skipped when the
autocomplete extension is not loaded and on Windows (requires a POSIX
pseudo-terminal).

Verified with a release shell build:

- Without the fix: test fails; history only contains `.exit` because the
completed line has no closing quote or semicolon and the statement stays
pending.
- With the fix: 28 autocomplete tests pass, including the new one;
related prompt and history tests also pass.

[#​2307](https://redirect.github.com/SBoudrias/Inquirer.js/pull/2307)).

- `search()` no longer submits a stale choice when Enter is pressed
while an async search is still loading — the prompt waits for the fresh
results, the query is preserved, and repeated Enter presses during
validation no longer run the async validator more than once
(`@inquirer/search`,

[#​2290](https://redirect.github.com/SBoudrias/Inquirer.js/issues/2290)).

    project.

    are deprecated: they still work and print a warning on stderr naming the
    --remote form. --local does nothing and warns. v4 removes all of

    appear in help.
  • --remote= can't be combined with any of the deprecated flags.
    --project-ref on a database command no longer needs --linked. An
    empty --project-ref= is now an error instead of being ignored.
    --password only applies to a hosted target.
  • db diff rejects --remote together with --from/--to; use
    --from=remote or --to=remote.
  • db query rejects SQL passed both as an argument and with --file.
  • Bare --remote (and the deprecated --linked) opens the project
    picker in an interactive terminal when the checkout isn't linked.
    Database and storage commands used to fail.
  • --remote after a command that takes an operand fails with a
    "did you mean" error when is, or is close to, a branch name of
    the linked project, when it's shaped like a project ref, or when the
    branch list can't be fetched. Put the operand before --remote
    (supabase db pull add_profiles --remote) or use --remote=.

    HostedMutationConsentRequiredError in non-interactive, JSON,
    stream-json, agent or -o json|yaml|toml|env runs unless --yes (or

    this for unattended runs:

    except with --dry-run

    • db query against a hosted target (or pass --read-only for reads)
    • seed buckets and storage cp/mv/rm against a hosted target
    • functions deploy/delete; secrets set/unset; config push
    • branches create/delete/disable/pause/unpause/update; backups restore

    • postgres-config update/delete; sso add/update/remove

  • [inbucket] and [remotes..inbucket] are

ci(cli): add a full benchmark for integration-heavy commands (#7412)

Adds the second tier of the CLI benchmark: the commands that need a
running local stack or
database. It stays report only; it never blocks a merge and is not a
required check.

- **`/bench full`** on a pull request (same permission rules as
`/bench`) dispatches the full
workflow on the pull request's branch and re-measures the
integration-heavy benchmark. It
refreshes the lightweight benchmark comment only when that comment is
behind the head commit. It
replies when a run is already in progress, when the branch has no full
benchmark workflow yet, or
  when the pull request is a draft, from a fork, or not into `develop`.
- **Actions UI**: `workflow_dispatch` on any branch with `workloads`,
`runtime`, and `base`
(the merge base, or a release tag). The job summary always has the
report; the pull request
comments are updated when the base is the merge base and the branch has
exactly one open pull
  request into `develop`.
- **Weekly schedule** (Sunday, off-peak) on `develop` against the latest
stable release, resolved at
run time. The report goes to the job summary and artifacts. Slack
notifications come later, once
  the data proves valid and useful.
- **Comments**: the integration-heavy benchmark posts its own comment,
separate from the existing
lightweight benchmark comment. Each comment shows the commit it
measured, keeps its own previous
runs, and ends with a note on which command re-runs it. Writes to each
comment are serialized per
  pull request.
- **Workloads**: stack lifecycle (`start`, `status`, `stop`, `db start`,
and `stack start|status|stop`), database work against the local stack
(`db reset`, `db query`, `test db`,
`gen types` at three schema sizes, `db diff` cold and warm, `db dump`,
`db lint`), and migrations
(`migration up`, `db push --local`, `migration list`). Migration
workloads add their migrations
  after the stack starts, so the measured command applies them.
- **Runtimes**: Docker and the native backend on Linux x64. Workloads
are packed into shards of
roughly ten minutes; base and branch alternate on one runner, and one
workload runs at a time.
- **Metrics**: wall time, phase deltas, Management API counts, container
operation counts, and
  binary size. Benchmark runs never send product telemetry.

Changed: `apps/cli/scripts/bench-cli.ts`, `bench-report.ts`,
`bench-summary.ts`,
`.github/workflows/cli-bench.yml`, `.github/scripts/cli-bench/*`, and
`apps/cli/docs/tracing-monitoring.md`. Added:
`.github/workflows/cli-bench-full.yml`,
`.github/scripts/cli-bench/full-plan.ts`,
`apps/cli/scripts/bench-pack.ts`, `bench-merge.ts`,
`bench-fixtures.ts`, and `apps/cli/bench/` (the full benchmark manifest
and fixtures).

GitHub runs dispatch, schedule, and comment-triggered workflows only
from the default branch, so the
workflow's actual runs (the Actions UI dispatch, `/bench full`, and the
schedule) cannot be tested
before this merges to `develop`. They get their first real run after the
merge.

ci(release): wait for platform packages before publishing the umbrella (#7417)

Every release has a window where installing `supabase` from npm on macOS
or Windows gives you the umbrella package with no binary. npm makes a
version installable a while after the publish returns, and the large
platform tarballs take longer than the small umbrella. On 3.0.0-beta.16
the umbrella was installable about a minute after publishing, but
`@supabase/cli-darwin-arm64` and `@supabase/cli-windows-x64` took four
to five minutes. npm skips a missing optional dependency without
failing, so `supabase.js` then throws `No matching Supabase CLI binary
package found`. The setup-cli@v3 smoke test in the Release workflow hit
exactly this.

`publish.ts` now polls the install packument for every platform package
and only publishes the umbrella once all of them are installable. It
checks every 10 seconds for up to 15 minutes, and gives up on a hung
probe after 30 seconds. If a package never shows up, the publish fails
before the umbrella goes out, and re-running it is safe because
already-published packages are skipped.

This touches release infrastructure and `v2.x` publishes the same way,
so it'll need a `backport/*` cherry-pick to `v2.x` too.

chore(repo): fix the API package sync and a CodeQL alert (#7416)

Two things have been turning develop's checks red.

1. The hourly API Package Sync has failed every run since 20 Oct. The
Management API spec now sets `contentEncoding: "binary"` on the ESZIP
upload body, and Effect's OpenAPI 3.0 converter rejects
`contentEncoding` and `contentMediaType` because they'd become active
keywords in Draft 2020-12. Both are only annotations and `format:
binary` already says the same thing, so `sanitizeOpenApiSchema` now
drops them. Once this lands, the next sync run should open the backlog
PR for `@supabase/api`.
2. CodeQL flags `js/incomplete-sanitization` in
`apps/cli/scripts/publish.ts`, because `name.replace("/", "%2F")` only
replaces the first slash. It shows up on every develop commit through
the production deploy PR. It's `replaceAll` now - no package name has
more than one slash, so there's no behaviour change.

`v2.x` has the same `publish.ts` line. With no behaviour change I don't
think it needs a backport, unless we want the alert cleared there too.

## Summary

Adds two properties to every CLI analytics event, `cli_command_executed`
included:

- `is_eval` is `true` when `SUPABASE_EVAL` is `1` or `true`

detection that already drives `is_agent` and the `feedback add`
metadata, so usage can be split by harness without decoding
`env_signals`.

Events from earlier CLI versions don't carry `is_eval`, so queries
should treat a missing value as `false`. Both properties are documented
in `apps/cli/docs/analytics.md`.

ci(cli): publish config schemas to supabase.com from stable releases (CLI-2864) (#7397)

## Summary

Since #7366 the config, project-config and `supabase.lock` schemas have
`$id`s under `https://supabase.com/schemas/`, but nothing serves them
yet. supabase/supabase#52509 sets up `apps/www/public/schemas` in
supabase/supabase, and this publishes to it from every stable release.

- New `scripts/publish-schemas.ts` copies the newest version of each
schema in `apps/docs/public/schemas` to `apps/www/public/schemas` on a
`cli/schemas` branch in supabase/supabase. It only opens a PR (or reuses
the open one) when a file changed, and arms auto-merge on it
- Before pushing, it checks that each schema is a JSON object, declares
draft-07, and has an `$id` matching the URL it'll be served from. Lower
versions are never written, and it refuses to publish if supabase.com
already serves a newer version or the `cli/schemas` branch changes
anything else, so a published version can't be modified
- `--dry-run` validates and prints what it would publish without
touching supabase/supabase. Release dry runs pass it
- The clone, branch, commit and PR steps move into
`scripts/publish-pull-request.ts`, shared with `publish-docs-spec.ts`.
The CLI reference publisher behaves the same as before
- The release `docs` job is now "Publish to supabase.com" and runs both
publishers, each without stopping the other. A failed publish adds an
error annotation and a step summary line, turns the job red and posts to
Slack (new `publish-failure` message). The release itself still succeeds

Auto-merge still waits on a code-owner approval, since supabase/supabase
`master` requires one and the releaser App can't approve its own PR. The
schemas path is owned by `@supabase/cli`, so one of us approves and it
merges itself. Making it fully hands-off would need the App added as a
bypass actor on that ruleset.

There's no `v*.x` branch at the minute, so no cherry-pick is needed.

## Linked issue

Closes CLI-2864

feat(config): add [auth.email] and [auth.sms] enabled, deprecating enable_signup (#7398)

## Summary

`enable_signup` under `[auth.email]` and `[auth.sms]` doesn't control
signups. `config push` sends it as `external_email_enabled` /
`external_phone_enabled`, which turns the whole provider on or off. So
setting `[auth.email] enable_signup = false` to stop new signups also
stops every existing user signing in with email (password, magic link or
OTP), which is what #7055 ran into. The key that blocks new signups is
`[auth] enable_signup`.

This adds `enabled` as the new name for both keys and deprecates
`enable_signup` in those two sections. The old key goes away in v4.

- `[auth.email] enabled` and `[auth.sms] enabled` are new, including
under `[remotes..auth.email]` and `[remotes..auth.sms]`. If
a section sets both, `enabled` wins.
- While a config still uses the old key, loading it prints a warning on
stderr, e.g. `WARN: auth.email.enable_signup is deprecated and will be
removed in v4, use auth.email.enabled instead.`
- `config push` and `config diff` print a warning when a change turns
the email or phone provider off, and point at `[auth] enable_signup` for
blocking new signups only. Push prints it before its confirmation
question.
- `config pull` writes whichever key the file already uses, and
`enabled` when it adds the key.
- `supabase init` writes `enabled`.
- The schema descriptions for these keys and for `[auth] enable_signup`
now say what each one does.

`enable_signup` stays the name in the decoded config, `ProjectConfig`,
the API mapping and the `config diff` / `config pull` JSON `path` until
v4, so nothing changes for `@supabase/config` consumers or JSON output.
`config pull`'s `document_path` names the key it actually wrote.

### Not covered

- `config diff` and `config push` still label the row
`auth.email.enable_signup` even when the file uses `enabled`. Renaming
the canonical path belongs with removing the old key (CLI-2892).

## Linked issue

Closes #7055 (CLI-2658)

Release Notes

Patch release: documentation. Commands, flags and output are unchanged.

  • The README walks from install to sign-in to a first real order: market data,

    after a network error. The network entry in agents/error-catalog.json
    names the lookup for each kind of write, Earn moves included, and the Earn
    skill records the allocation before each move so that a timed-out call can be
    checked.
  • Market counts in the README and agent docs match the live listings: 170+

    start a local server.
  • The MCP docs and the setup skills warn that the feedback tool can upload a
    local file it names, with no approval step. Drop feedback from -s for an
    agent that reads untrusted input.
  • Smaller corrections across the auth, MCP and streaming docs, such as
    auth reset deleting every stored key and record capturing market-data
    channels only.

Verifying GitHub Artifact Attestations

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the GitHub CLI:

You can also download the attestation from GitHub and verify against that directly:

Release Notes

Sign in from the browser, run the MCP server and the REPL as their own binaries,
take a paper strategy live, and package a finished session as a recipe. The
catalog lists 188 commands in 15 groups; kraken-mcp serves 152 of them as MCP
tools. The project is still alpha: test with paper trading first.

Upgrading from 0.4.1

These changes need action from scripts, agents or MCP clients.

  • The MCP server and the REPL are separate binaries. Use kraken-mcp
    instead of kraken mcp and kraken-shell instead of kraken shell. Run the
    installer again before you update an agent plugin: the plugins now start
    kraken-mcp. In a client config, -s and --allow-dangerous work as before;
    pass API keys as KRAKEN_API_KEY and KRAKEN_API_SECRET in the client's
    environment. After a source install, run
    cargo uninstall kraken-mcp kraken-shell before installing kraken-cli.
  • REST output carries the fields the CLI models. Fields Kraken adds are no
    longer passed through. query-orders returns the same order shape as
    open-orders, query-trades the same fill shape as trades-history, and
    auth test reports balances like balance. JSON objects keep the server's
    order instead of sorting keys.
  • MCP tool calls. A dangerous call goes to the operator through MCP
    elicitation; acknowledged: true applies only to clients that cannot show
    one. Results larger than 256 KiB are refused with the arguments that narrow
    them, results over 16 KiB come back as structuredContent only, and a result
    that is not a JSON object arrives as {"result": ...}.
  • Catalog schema 2.0.0. parameters became input_schema (JSON Schema),
    auth_required became credentials, global_flags is gone, and positional
    arguments moved from command to usage. New fields: effect, reach,
    tool, why and constraints.
  • kraken record writes JSONL by default. It wrote DuckDB before. Pass
    --to duckdb (or --to duckdb,jsonl) to keep appending to a 0.4.x DuckDB
    tape. Release binaries read and write DuckDB; a source build needs
    --features record-duckdb to do either.
  • Futures paper accounts. Open orders saved by 0.4.1 use the old type
    spelling and are not migrated: delete /paper/futures_state.json
    and run kraken futures paper init.
  • The Claude Code plugin no longer asks for an API key. Its tools need none,
    and it no longer passes a key saved under 0.4.x to kraken-mcp; kraken-mcp
    still reads the active key stored by kraken auth set or kraken auth login.
  • kraken feedback keeps no local copy. Its output no longer has id and
    path; you can delete /feedback.duckdb.

New commands

Command What it does
kraken auth login Sign in in the browser; saves a restricted, expiring Spot API key
kraken auth switch api-key|sign-in Choose which stored key signs requests
kraken recipe create|list|show|run Package a stopped paper session and run it again
kraken plugin init|list Scaffold a dependency-free extension over the CLI's JSON output
kraken lab curve The full marked equity series behind lab score
kraken-mcp, kraken-shell The MCP server and the REPL, installed next to kraken

auth login needs a terminal, so a script or an agent cannot create a key. The
key has no withdrawal rights and expires after 90 days unless --valid-for says
less; --read-only creates a key that cannot trade, and --no-browser only
prints the sign-in URL. auth reset deletes the local copy only: delete the key
in the Kraken UI to revoke it at once. An older release ignores the sign-in key
and can drop it from config.toml, so delete it in the Kraken UI before you
downgrade.

Changed commands

  • workspace create --mode live and workspace promote now work. A live
    workspace is a budget-fenced allocation of the real account: creation checks
    the allocation against the real balance, orders print a live banner on stderr,
    and venue fills are reconciled by transaction ID.
  • ticker --all returns every tradable pair, ticker --watch streams
    snapshots as NDJSON, and one call can mix asset classes.
  • Orders are checked before they reach Kraken: a Spot *-limit order needs
    price2, a futures order takes only the prices its type uses, and sizes and
    prices must be decimals.
  • auth show (alias auth status) names the key in use and says when a flag or
    an environment variable overrides it.
  • kraken setup without a terminal fails with a validation error that names
    KRAKEN_API_KEY and KRAKEN_API_SECRET. setup and auth set refuse an API
    secret that is not valid base64.
  • session show includes the strategy label and parameters. Streams print a
    reconnected event on stdout after a reconnect.
  • With -o json, commands that write their own output no longer print a
    trailing {}.

Fixed

  • A timed-out order, cancel, withdrawal or transfer is never sent again. When it
    may have executed (a timeout, a broken connection, a 5xx, or an accepted reply
    that does not decode), the error envelope carries "verify_first": true,

perf(sync): download block access lists for executed blocks in full sync (#15378)

* perf(sync): download block access lists for executed blocks in full sync

* perf(sync): execute at once when no peer serves block access lists

* perf(sync): skip access lists of executed blocks below the serving window

Below the serving window of the best known header peers may have pruned
the list, so each batch waited for retries that fail. The window now caps
a peer head at the best known header with beacon headers included.

* perf(sync): skip stored access lists and recheck list peers on each request

- Do not download the access list of a block whose list is already in the store,
  e.g. a beacon body from engine_newPayload.
- Share the predicate for "execution uses access lists" with the recovery step,
  so the zkEVM build does not download lists for parallel execution.
- Compute the no-list-peer skip again on each request, and require a list peer
  whose head is at or above the block, as the allocation strategy does.
- Count downloaded list bytes in the download buffer size.
- Do not say that sync cannot pass a block that can execute without its list.

* perf(sync): check the access list store once per buffered block

- Check the store for a block access list once, when the block enters
  the download buffer, and only for a header with a list hash. Before,
  each request read the store up to four times per header.
- A list that newPayload stores while a request is in flight no longer
  changes whether the block can execute without the list.
- Reset the list size estimate when no buffered block holds or needs a
  list, so it no longer limits the buffer after list downloads stop.

name of any existing config section with `profile X already exists.

`FieldByName`, which also finds one promoted from an embedded struct,
and used it for the outer struct's own fields. That list can only name

`resources.ClusterPolicy` `definition` /

Revert bundle file uploads to import-file and replace nodes of the other type (#7218)

## Changes

Fixes #7216.

- **Revert #7034 and #6149.** Bundle files are uploaded through the
legacy `import-file` endpoint again. `/workspace/import` behaves
differently from it in ways the CLI couldn't fully work around (summary:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yIaFyB6IoYGBuynPwQNnb6uwbcEznUZPaVY6AEl2iOw):
`AUTO` rejects reserved asset names, can't overwrite an extracted
`.zip`, and classifies notebooks differently. The CLI-side
classification added in #7034 to avoid `AUTO` imported some notebooks
(e.g. a SQL notebook starting with a byte order mark) as plain files.
- **Replace a node of the other type.** Overwrite can't change a node's
type: `import-file` returns 400 when a file holds the name of a notebook
upload, and 409 when a notebook holds the name of a file upload.
Deployments made with v1.21 and v1.22 have such files. When an overwrite
fails with one of those two collision messages, the filer deletes the
node of the other type (checked with `get-status`) and uploads once
more, so the remote matches the local file. Any other error is returned
as before.

Forward-fixes for changes on main since #6149: the `upload-504` tests
(#7014) and `upload/internal_server_error` inject faults on the
`import-file` URL again, the multipart request recorder stays (snapshot
uploads use it), and the testserver keeps the improvements from
#6149/#7034 (its `/workspace/import` model, `fault.py --body-contains`,
JUPYTER imports). `libs/notebook` is left as on main.

The testserver now also extracts a `.zip` sent to `import-file` into the
parent folder, like the real endpoint (`importZipFile` in universe),
instead of storing it as a file. The ssh tests therefore upload valid
placeholder archives instead of empty files.

Upload errors no longer carry the `failed to upload :` prefix
#6149 added; the path is still in the `Endpoint:` line, as in v1.20.

## Why

Discussed in Slack: revert until the backend fixes `/workspace/import`,
and clean up mismatched nodes client-side, since a deploy's goal is for
the remote to match the local files.

## Tests

- New `bundle/sync/replace-node-type` (`Cloud = true`): a file where the
upload is a notebook and a notebook where the upload is a file are both
replaced. Passes locally and on `aws-cli`.
- New `bundle/sync/zip-extract` (`Cloud = true`): a synced `.zip` is
extracted into the file path and overwritten on the next sync. Passes
locally and on `aws-cli`.

except the new `deleteNodeOfOtherType`. Deploying the same 32-file
bundle (notebook header variants, `.zip`, reserved asset names, a
dashboard) twice with released v1.20.0 and with this branch on dogfood
gives identical object types and byte-identical contents, and a deploy

description:
fix(databricks): validate views on ALTER and no-op runs like CREATE

* fix(databricks): validate views on ALTER and no-op runs like CREATE

Closes #16883

Resolves dbt-labs/dbt-core#16882

Ports [databricks/dbt-databricks#1736](https://github.com/databricks/dbt-databricks/pull/1736).

### Problem

With `use_materialization_v2` and `view_update_via_alter: true`, an existing Databricks view takes the ALTER or no-op path, which skips the checks `create_view_as` runs on CREATE/REPLACE:

- An enforced model contract is never checked, so a contract-breaking query is applied with `ALTER VIEW AS`, and a YAML-only contract change passes as a no-op.
- `column_mask` and `row_filter` configs, which CREATE rejects because Databricks does not support them on views, are silently ignored.

Separately, when the query changes, the ALTER path replays the pre-ALTER column-comment diff after `ALTER VIEW AS` has already reapplied documented comments. That diff can target columns the new query removed and fail with `UNRESOLVED_COLUMN`.

### Solution

Sync the vendored view macros with dbt-databricks:

- `create.sql`: move the mask, row filter, and contract checks into a `validate_view_model(sql)` macro, called by `databricks__create_view_as`.
- `materializations/view.sql`: call `validate_view_model(sql)` on the ALTER branch before any DDL, so ALTER and no-op runs fail the same way CREATE does.
- `alter.sql`: after a query change, reapply comments from the view's current columns and skip the pre-ALTER `column_comments` diff.

Models without an enforced contract run no extra queries; the mask and filter checks only read config.

**Tests:**

- `dbt-loader`: `v2_update_via_alter_rejects_unsupported_configs_without_changes` checks that an existing view with no changes still rejects a row filter and a column mask. `alter_view_query_change_reapplies_post_alter_comments_only` checks that a query change writes the post-ALTER comment and does not replay the stale pre-ALTER one.

description:
fix: exclude connection-limit wait time from run results execution time

* fix: exclude connection-limit wait time from run results execution time

Closes #16556

Resolves dbt-labs/dbt-core#15724

### Problem

Run results report wall-clock execution time, which includes the time a node
spends waiting on the connection-limit semaphore. That wait time is not
execution, so it inflates the execution time reported for each node.

### Solution

Track connection-limit idle time on the NodeEvaluated span and subtract it
from the wall-clock duration when run results are generated. The result
saturates at zero, so a node that waits longer than it runs reports zero, not
a negative duration.

  method that subtracts idle time
- dbt-tasks-sa: backfill `idle_time_ms` from the `NodeEvaluated` span onto the
  run result stat
- dbt-tasks-core: compute run results execution time via
  `get_execution_duration()`

Tests cover subtraction and zero-clamping.

description:
fix: return the group when indexing a modules.re match object

* fix: return the group when indexing a modules.re match object (#16451)

Closes #16485

Resolves dbt-labs/dbt-core#16451

### Problem

Indexing a match object from `modules.re.search` or `modules.re.match` (`m[0]`, `m[1]`, `m['name']`) renders an empty string without an error, while `m.group(1)` works. In dbt-core, `m[g]` is Python's `re.Match.__getitem__` and returns the same as `m.group(g)`.

`Capture::get_value` in `crates/dbt-jinja/minijinja-contrib/src/modules/re.rs` answered integer keys only for `re.findall` results and had no lookup by group name.

Reproduced on DuckDB with the project from the issue (`dbt compile`):

| Expression | dbt 2.0.6 / 2.0.7 | dbt-core 1.12.5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `m[0]`, `m[1]`, `m[2]`, `m["num"]` | empty | `order-42`, `order`, `42`, `42` |
| `m.group(2)` | `42` | `42` |

### Solution

- As suggested in the issue, integer keys now index the groups for match and search results too (`m[0]` is the whole match). `re.findall` results work as before.
- A string subscript checks the named groups first and then the attribute names, as in Python, while attribute access checks the attribute names first. With a group named `pos`, `m['pos']` is the group and `m.pos` stays the attribute. To tell the two apart, minijinja's `Object` trait gets a `get_item` hook for subscripts that defaults to `get_value`, so other objects are unchanged.
- Slicing, iteration and `len()` stay unsupported, as in Python.

Tested with `cargo nextest run -p minijinja-contrib` (new tests: `test_re_match_capture_index_access_returns_group`, `test_re_match_result_index_access_returns_group`, `test_re_match_capture_missing_group_is_undefined`, `test_re_match_capture_attributes_still_resolve`, `test_re_match_capture_group_named_like_attribute`) and `cargo nextest run -p minijinja` (new test: `test_object_get_item_overrides_subscript_only`). With a local build, the project from the issue renders `order-42`, `order`, `42`, `42`, and these cases also match dbt-core: `re.match` results, missing groups (`m[5]`, `m['nope']` and `m[-1]` render empty), `m.pos`, `m.string` and `m.lastgroup`, and groups named like those attributes (`p['pos']`, `p['string']`).

fix(benchmarks): preserve Game Arena leaderboard columns (#1236)

## Summary

While checking the `kaggle benchmarks leaderboard` command, I found that
most columns were missing from Game Arena leaderboards.

For `kaggle/game-arena`, only `Games Covered` was displayed. The `Score`
and `Matches Played` columns were missing from `--show`, `--download`,
and `--format json`.

The issue was that the CLI used `benchmark_task_slug` as the column key.
Game Arena returns an empty slug for all its metrics, so each column
overwrote the previous one in the dictionary, leaving only the last
column.

This also affected `chess-text` and `poker-heads-up`. `chess-suite` was
not affected because its task slugs are unique.

## Fix

I changed the column key to use both the task slug and task name. This
prevents columns with empty slugs from overwriting each other.

I also replaced `slug_to_field()` with generated field names (`task_0`,
`task_1`, etc.) so each column has its own internal identifier.

Columns now follow the order returned by the server instead of being
sorted alphabetically by slug. This keeps `Score` first on Game Arena.

The existing score formatting remains unchanged, and leaderboards with
unique slugs continue to work as before.

## Tests

Added `test_benchmark_leaderboard_cli_empty_task_slugs_keep_all_columns`
to cover the case where multiple columns have empty task slugs.

The test fails with the old implementation and passes with this fix.

Ran:

- `pytest tests/unit/test_benchmarks_leaderboard.py
tests/unit/test_cli_benchmarks.py`
- `pytest tests/unit`

Results:

- 53 passed
- 1435 passed, 48 subtests passed

Also checked the live API responses for `game-arena`, `chess-text`,
`poker-heads-up`, and `chess-suite` using `--show`, and checked
`game-arena` with `--download` and `--format json`.

fix(live,trading): prevent CPU busy-wait spinning during stream startup (#762) (#781)

DataStream and TradingStream already suspend startup on an asyncio.Event
until a subscription arrives (#837) instead of polling the event loop.
stop_ws() still called Event.set() directly after enqueueing the stop
message. That set runs on the caller's thread, so it does not wake a loop
blocked in another thread. An idle stream started on a background thread
and stopped from the main thread waited forever, even though the stop
message was already on the queue.

stop_ws() now enqueues the stop message and then calls
_wake_subscription_wait(), which schedules the wake on the stream's own
loop with call_soon_threadsafe. TradingStream.stop_ws() also yields once,
matching DataStream.

Tests cover wake-on-subscribe, idle stop, and the case where
cancelErrors/corrections alone do not start a DataStream. Cross-thread
tests subscribe and stop from a different loop after the stream is actually
idle, which is the path that used to hang.

The original busy-wait in #762 was fixed by #837. This is the leftover
cross-thread stop hang.

fix(cli): delimit config paths with $PATH's own separator (#800)

* fix(cli): delimit config paths with $PATH's own separator

On Windows an absolute path carries a colon of its own, so `-c
C:\Users\me\config.toml` was split on it and read as the two paths `C` and
`\Users\me\config.toml`. Neither exists, so the configuration was never
found and every command failed with "No configuration found", even though
the file was there. The same held for HIMALAYA_CONFIG, which feeds the
same argument.

The separator is now `;` on Windows, as `$PATH` and `std::env::split_paths`
spell it, and stays `:` elsewhere, so nothing changes on Unix. Several
paths can still be given at once, and a single one is never split.

* docs(config): state the platform config path separator

The loader now splits -c on \'s own separator, so the README, the sample configuration and the config spec say so, and an Unreleased entry records the Windows fix and the colon-joined trade-off that comes with it.

* test(cli): pin the config path delimiter to the platform

The two splitting tests build their input from the constant, so an unconditional semicolon would pass them on Unix while breaking every colon-joined path there. Assert the constant itself.

description:
feat(apps): add +features and +feature-enable for app business features (#2816)

* feat(apps): add +features and +feature-enable for app business features

Apps can now turn on server-side business features from the CLI. The
first one is pg (the app database), so a full_stack app no longer has to
be created with a database or upgraded through a cloud session to get
one.

- +features lists each feature's name and enabled flag
  (GET /open-apis/spark/v1/apps/:app_id/features). With --operation-ref it
  also reports the enable operation kept for that key.
- +feature-enable --feature pg posts only an idempotent_key. Network
  failures are replayed with the same key; --idempotent-key resumes an
  earlier attempt from the operation the server keeps for it; a running
  operation is polled for at most 60s without re-sending the write. A
  40913 answer looks up the operation kept for this key first, so a
  replay that races its own first attempt is followed instead of being
  reported as a conflict.
- Studio error codes (also behind the gateway's 33xxxxx form) are
  explained: 40914 not a new-contract app (enable the database in Miaoda
  cloud development), 40915 the key can no longer be used (check
  +features, then start over without --idempotent-key), 40001, 40009,
  40912, 40913 and 42900 get their own subtype and hint. Only outcomes
  that may still change point at the --operation-ref query.
- next_steps after a successful enable depend on where the command runs:
  inside a Miaoda sandbox (MIAODA_AUTHN_CODE is set) the platform applies
  the database; locally it is +env-pull and a restart of the dev process.
- +env-pull applies the pg keys explicitly: an explicit disable clears
  the connection keys and FORCE_DB_BRANCH, an exported connection pins
  FORCE_DB_BRANCH=dev, and it reports restart_required and shell
  variables that would shadow .env.local (names only).
- Keys are sent in the lower-case form the server stores.
- lark-apps skill, references and the apps E2E coverage table cover the
  new commands.

* fix(apps): report a server without the app features API as final

A server that does not implement the app features API answers every call
through the OpenAPI gateway with HTTP 500 and code 2200 "Internal
Error". The CLI classified that as a retryable server error, and
+feature-enable told the caller to resume the same key, so an agent
pointed at such a server kept retrying a call that cannot succeed.

The gateway gives the same answer for a passing upstream failure and the
response carries nothing that tells the two apart, so a 2200 from the
feature endpoints is now re-checked with one plain read of the features
endpoint. Only when that read fails the same way is the error reported
as feature_not_available, not retryable, with a hint to upgrade the
server or enable the database in Miaoda cloud development. A re-check
that succeeds keeps the original error and its same-key resume guidance;
for +features the successful second read is simply returned.

* fix(apps): ask for re-authorization instead of a same-key resume on credential failures

An authentication failure on +feature-enable, on the key lookup before a
resume, or on +features --operation-ref used to fall through to the
recovery for outcomes that may still change, so the caller was told to
resume the same idempotent_key. No key can succeed until the user
authorizes again, and an agent following that hint kept retrying.

- Code 221801 ("miaoda UAT expired and cannot refresh, need
  reactivate"), which the Miaoda sandbox proxy returns once the user
  credential can no longer be refreshed, is classified as
  authentication / token_expired next to 221800, so it exits as an
  authentication error and is not retryable.
- The feature commands now handle any authentication failure the same
  way the CLI's missing-login error does: not retryable, and with the
  standard user-authorization recovery when the producer left no hint.
  That recovery is projected per distribution, so builds without
  `auth login` keep the generic re-authorization wording.

* fix(apps): treat a proxy's bare HTTP 401 as an authentication failure

The Miaoda sandbox proxy answers a credential it cannot accept with HTTP
401 and its own JSON body ({"status_code":"k_gw_ec_000032",...}), not a
Spark envelope. The shared classifier turns such a status into an api
error with code 401, so +feature-enable still told the caller to resume
the same idempotent_key and +features pointed at the app id.

Spark answers its own failures inside an envelope and neither the
features service nor the OpenAPI plugin answers with HTTP 401, so a bare
401 reaching these commands is a credential rejected in front of Spark.
On the enable, the key lookup before a resume and +features it is now
re-typed as an authentication error (token_invalid, code 401) and gets
the same handling as code 221801: not retryable, with the standard
user-authorization recovery. +export already maps its 401 the same way.

* refactor(apps): name the app database feature "database"

The feature name says what the app gets rather than which engine backs it,
matching how the db-* commands refer to the app's database. The CLI accepts
only `--feature database`; `pg` is rejected during validation.

* test(apps): expect the database feature name in the +features pretty output

* fix(apps): treat a gateway 404 for the app features routes as final

Before the app features routes are registered on an OpenAPI gateway, every
call to them is answered with a bare HTTP 404 ("404 page not found", no API
envelope). +features reported it as an app-not-found error pointing at the
app list, and +feature-enable offered a same-key resume that can only
repeat the 404.

A bare 404 is now recognized next to the gateway's internal error (2200):
after one read-only re-check answered the same way, both commands report
feature_not_available, not retryable, and point at Miaoda cloud development.
When only the enable is answered with a 404 while the features read works,
the enable is final as well instead of offering a resume. Spark answers its
own failures, a missing app included, inside an envelope, so a bare 404 only
comes from the gateway.

* fix(apps): recognize the gateway's plain-text 404 for the features routes

The gateway answers an unregistered route with "404 page not found". Its
leading 404 decodes as a JSON number, so the response classifier reports an
internal "non-object JSON response" error rather than an HTTP 404: on the
production gateway +features exited 5 with an app-list hint, and the
previous change did not match it.

A non-object JSON response now counts as an answer that did not come from
the API, next to a bare 404 and the gateway's internal error (2200). After
the read-only re-check, both commands re-type it as an API error and report
feature_not_available, so the exit code is 1 instead of 5. Tests now use the
gateway's real 404 body and also cover a 404 body that does not decode.

* docs: keep the top-level README apps row unchanged

The app features commands are documented in the lark-apps skill; the top-level
README only summarizes each domain.

* docs(apps): decide the frontend local-dev flow by the app type the server returns

A frontend create can come back as a full_stack app without a database; such an
app enables its database with +features / +feature-enable instead of going to
Miaoda cloud development.

* fix(apps): keep the key on unverifiable enable answers and bound the wait

- A body that is no API envelope is only taken for a missing route when the
  HTTP status is 404. A 200 with a null body leaves open whether the enable
  was applied: the command reads the operation kept for its key and reports
  it, and otherwise keeps the key, the read-only query and the same-key resume.
- The 60s wait limit now covers the poll reads: each read and its network
  replays run under the wait deadline, and an answer that arrives after it
  is reported as the wait timeout with the original key.
- A rate-limited enable leaves no operation for its key, so the hint asks for
  a new attempt without --idempotent-key, like any key the server does not
  keep; following it completes the enable.
- Describe an older app's custom variables without internal configuration
  system names.

* fix(apps): keep the key when a replay or a resume is rate limited

A rate limit only says the limited request did nothing. After a network
replay, or on a resume, the key may already name an operation, so the key is
read first: an operation the resume rule would not re-send is reported as it
is, a retryable failure keeps the key for a later resume, and only the
server's own "not kept" answer leads to a new attempt without
--idempotent-key. A first request that is rate limited keeps the new-attempt
hint.

description:
fix(apps): tell git to quit when the credential helper cannot answer (#2854)

* fix(apps): tell git to quit when the credential helper cannot answer

When the git credential helper manages a repository URL but cannot supply a
credential (expired or missing user token, refresh failure, login mismatch,
unreadable input or config), it only wrote the error to stderr and returned
nothing. git then fell through to its interactive username/password prompt
or GIT_ASKPASS, which never returns in a non-interactive agent session, so
`git push` hung instead of failing with the helper's explanation.

The helper now answers such requests with `quit=1`, which tells git to stop
consulting helpers and not to prompt, so the git command fails immediately
and the stderr explanation is the last thing the caller sees. URLs that have
no lark-cli credential record still get an empty answer, so other helpers
keep working for repositories lark-cli does not manage.

* test(apps): cover a failed credential write in the git helper

Get returns the write error and does not append quit=1 after a partially
written credential.

* fix(apps): only quit for URLs with a lark-cli credential record

Requests the helper cannot map to a managed URL (unsupported protocol,
missing host, missing app id, unreadable input, config errors) now get an
empty answer again, as on main, so other credential helpers can still
answer them. quit=1 is reserved for URLs that have a lark-cli record but no
usable credential, which is where git otherwise fell through to a prompt.

* fix(apps): stay silent when the credential store cannot be read

A failed store read has not shown that lark-cli manages the URL, so the
helper leaves the request to other helpers instead of answering quit=1.
readConfirmed now returns the found record with a login-mismatch error so
that case, where a record does exist, still quits.

* refactor(apps): unexport writeGitQuit now that only the helper uses it

* fix(auth): explain logins that receive no refresh_token

The token endpoint only issues a refresh_token when the app has turned on
"Refresh user_access_token" in its security settings and published an app
version containing that change. Requesting offline_access is not enough, and
the endpoint still echoes offline_access in the granted scope, so a login
without a refresh_token looked successful and then forced a new
authorization two hours later with no explanation.

- auth login: when no refresh_token is issued, print a warning with the
  expiry time, the cause and the security-settings URL; the JSON
  authorization_complete payload gains refresh_token_issued, expires_at and
  a no_refresh_token object (cause, fix, settings_url)
- auth status: a still-valid token without a refresh_token reports when it
  will stop working and how to make future logins renewable
- expired token without refresh_token: the need_user_authorization hint and
  the auth status diagnosis name the refresh setting and link to it; the
  error subtype is unchanged

* fix(identitydiag): keep the no-refresh-token warning after --verify

A successful verification overwrote the ready message with a plain
"User identity: ready", dropping the expiry warning for logins that
received no refresh_token. Ready identities now keep the message computed
before verification.

* fix(auth): keep profile-aware login recovery when no refresh_token was issued

The expired-without-refresh_token error used a fixed `lark-cli auth login`
hint, so a command run with --profile pointed the user at the default
profile and lost the --no-wait / --device-code login flow that the generic
missing-token error gives. Compose the explanation with the standard
UserAuthorization recovery instead.

* fix(identitydiag): omit refreshExpiresAt for logins without a refresh_token

The device flow stores the access-token expiry as the refresh expiry when
no refresh_token is issued, so diagnostics reported a refresh expiry for a
token that cannot be renewed. Report refreshExpiresAt only when a refresh
token exists; the stored token is unchanged.

* fix(whoami): surface the no-refresh-token warning for available identities

whoami dropped the diagnosis message and only passed the hint through for
unavailable identities, so a user token that works now but cannot be
renewed showed only available/ready. Add a message field and pass the user
hint through whenever the diagnosis provides one.

* docs(lark-shared): relay the no-refresh-token login warning to the user

After the split-flow login completes, tell the user when no refresh_token
was issued. Only an app admin can turn on "Refresh user_access_token" and
publish a version, so an agent that silently re-authorizes every two hours
leaves the cause hidden.

description:
Fix streamable HTTP memory leak from unstable OpenAPI spec object identity (#335)

Every new HTTP session called initProxy(), which re-read and JSON.parse()'d
the OpenAPI spec from disk, producing a fresh object each time. openapi-client-axios
dereferences that document through dereference-json-schema, which caches its
(expensive, fully-expanded) output in a process-lifetime Map keyed by the
input object's identity, with no eviction. A fresh object on every call
defeated that cache on every session and permanently retained a full
dereferenced copy of the spec, forever.

Cache the parsed spec by (specPath, baseUrl) so repeated sessions share the
same object identity, letting the upstream cache actually hit instead of
growing unbounded. Verified with heap snapshots: an isolated initProxy() loop
went from +23.2MB/300 calls to +237KB/300 calls (98% reduction, remainder is
one-time JIT warmup, not a leak), and a full end-to-end run (server as a
separate process, sessions properly terminated via DELETE) plateaus after an
initial JIT warmup with no further growth between 100 and 300 cycles.

Fixes #144

fix(mcp): the agent CLI is resolved through PATH before launching

`mcp install` for the agent target started the helper process with the
bare command name. On macOS and Linux .NET resolves that relative to the
working directory before consulting PATH, so the launch failed with "No

installer fell back to the manual instructions.

(honouring PATHEXT on Windows so `.cmd` wrappers are found) and launches

description:
[v1.1.0] - 2026-10-30

This release is the first minor version bump since the v1.0.x line. Highlights:

  1. A brand-new update subcommand group that plugs into the server-side "version-info push + user remind preference" mechanism, covering interactive check / query / preference-set / self-upgrade, and additionally injecting a top-level _notice.update prompt into every command response (gated by user preference and a throttle window).
  2. record subcommand group consolidation and expansion: the 8 shipped record subcommands, together with a batch of new capabilities (sharing-config read/write, grant-member management, smart-recording config, structured todos, AI timeline, ...), are collapsed into 6 subcommands dispatched via --action.

Added

  • New update subcommand group (cmd/update/): wires up /v1/cli/version-info and friends, end-to-end covering "check latest → user decides → download + verify + install → persist preference". All four subcommands require login.
    • update check — reports current version, server-advertised latest version, whether an upgrade is actionable (combining blacklist), and the user's current preference. Returns a fully-populated CheckInfo even in the "already latest" case so the Agent sees a stable shape.
    • update get — pure-local inspection of the persisted preference and the most recent cache, intended for diagnostics.
    • update set --preference remind|never_remind — the local file is written first as the authoritative source, then a best-effort report is sent to the server-side never_remind allowlist; upload failures are only logged and never propagated so a transient network blip does not loop the Agent through repeated retries.
    • update run — the actual upgrade entry point: enforces cross-process single-flight via filelock.ProcessLock; default path is "download the CDN tgz → npm install -g ", and when the server flips target_from_npm=true it falls through to npm install -g @tencentcloud/tmeet@. On Windows the "replace the running exe" problem is solved by npm's postinstall shim, so Linux / macOS / Windows share a single code path.
  • Automatic _notice.update injection (internal/output/print.go, internal/notice/): every success response rendered via FormatPrint automatically appends a top-level _notice.update payload (opt-out via the new WithoutUpdateNotice() option). The shape of the injection is decided jointly by the local preference (unset / remind / never_remind), the server-advertised notice_gap throttle window, and the feedback-channel special case; within one window each account is prompted at most once.
  • New record capabilities (cmd/record/):
    • record share-set — a single call can simultaneously "update sharing config + batch add members + batch remove members". The CLI dispatches to the relevant downstream APIs as needed and aggregates succeeded / failed / results[] so partial-success outcomes are visible without ambiguity. Core flags cover the sharing master switch, the permission-point mode (1~6: public / corp × view / password / approve), access password, expiration type and custom expiration time, viewer-download / view-transcript-and-minutes / Rooms-visibility toggles, and member add/remove. Write operation; added to the dangerous-operation confirmation table.
    • record settings-set — modifies the record file's "subtitle switch" and "AI smart-recording switch" (1 = off / 2 = on); at least one of the two flags must be provided, and Flags().Changed(...) ensures unchanged fields are not sent. Write operation.
    • record access --action sharing|members|settings — query sharing config, authorized members, or smart-recording config (previously only address was supported).
    • record content --action todos|timeline — structured smart-todos retrieval and AI smart-timeline retrieval; transcript / minutes additionally gain the "paginated list by share URL" form.
    • record search --query-field grows two new values: todo (search smart-minutes todo content) and smart_minutes (includes todos).
  • New internal/upgrade upgrade-primitives package (internal/upgrade/): a cobra-free toolkit extracted from cmd/update so it can be reused by future commands or test harnesses.
    • DownloadToTemp — 10-minute wall-clock timeout combined with a 60-second idle timeout, honors context cancellation, shares a package-level *http.Client for connection pooling, and computes SHA-256 inline while streaming.
    • InstallSkill + SkillInstallPath — downloads the skills zip archive, verifies the checksum, extracts into a staging directory, then atomically swaps it into place via a rename-rename-remove sequence. Any failure rolls back; there is no window where the final path points at half-extracted contents. The payload format is also switched from tarball to zip.
    • RunNpmInstall — wraps npm install -g with explicit npm_config_prefix injection (so a stray ~/.npmrc cannot redirect installs), a 15-second "still installing" heartbeat tick, and captures the tail of npm's output on failure as a diagnostic.
    • ResolveNpmPrefix — prefers env vars such as TMEET_NPM_PACKAGE_DIR, falling back to npm root -g, so the global install location stays consistent with where the CLI actually lives.
    • Full unit tests for the whole package.
  • New internal/notice notice-and-preference package (internal/notice/): centralises every "CLI upgrade prompt" policy decision without taking a reverse dependency on internal/output.
    • Three assembly entry points: BuildWithOutcome / AssembleForCheck / BuildForFeedback. The throttle "window" is simply the filecache envelope's own TTL — there is no separate "last_notified_at" field.
    • CompareVersion / IsNewer use segment-based pre-release comparison, so v1.1.0-beta.3 and v1.1.0-rc.1 order correctly against each other.
    • LoadPreference / SavePreference persist to ~/.tmeet/data//preference.json.
  • cmdutil.ActionRegistry / FlagRule / SingleStringVar (internal/cmdutil/action.go, flags.go, single_string.go): the --action dispatch framework. Each action declares its own ApiCmd / FlagRules / Validate / Run, and the framework uniformly enforces flag rejection, resolves the api cmd, and dispatches. Unconditional and conditional rules live in the same FlagRules table; rule-table bugs surface at test time as internal errors rather than silently masking unrelated flags. SingleStringVar makes --action-style flags fail command parsing when passed twice instead of silently taking the last value.
  • Eight new record-related enums and converters (internal/utils/enumerate/): RecordPermissionPoint / RecordMemberPermission / RecordExpiredTimeType / RecordCorpShareScope / RecordSettingType / SmartMinutesType / RecordingTimelineStatus / TranscriptType, consumed by the new record commands for output field translation and input validation.
  • New exception codes (internal/exception/): UpdateLockError / UpdateServerPayloadError / UpdateDownloadError / UpdateTempFileError / UpdateChecksumError / UpdateNpmMissingError / UpdateNpmInstallError / UpdateExtractError / UpdateInstallError / UpdatePreferenceSaveError.
  • npm uninstall helper script (scripts/uninstall.js): standalone, idempotent three-step cleanup — stop the event bus daemon → run tmeet auth logout through the official logout path (which fires ResourceReleaseHooks) → remove TMEET_CLI_CONFIG_DIR (defaults to ~/.tmeet/). Any failing step only logs and never aborts the next step. README gains an "Uninstall" section.

Changed

  • record subcommand group fully restructured (cmd/record/base.go): the 8 shipped record subcommands, together with the new capabilities added in this release (sharing-config read/write, grant-member management, smart-recording config, structured todos, AI timeline, ...), are consolidated into 6 --action-dispatched commands — search / content --action / access --action / share-set / settings-set / permission-apply --action. Mapping of the 8 shipped subcommands to the new surface:
    • record list + record search → record search
    • record address → record access --action address
    • record smart-minutes → record content --action minutes
    • record transcript-get → record content --action transcript
    • record transcript-search → record content --action transcript --text ...
    • record transcript-paragraphs → record content --action paragraphs
    • record permission-apply-prepare → record permission-apply --action prepare
    • record permission-apply-commit → record permission-apply --action commit
  • Default time-window behaviour of meeting search / meeting list-ended / minutes search / record search is now documented inline: the server-side fallback used when both --start and --end are omitted is spelled out in --help (list-ended: last 30 days / meeting search: 30 days before and after now / minutes search: last 1 year / record search: last 30 days).
  • Minutes terminology unified (cmd/minutes/get.go, SKILL references/tmeet-minutes.md): "steady-state / transient" → "global summary / real-time summary", aligning with the Yuanbao product terminology ("global minutes vs. real-time minutes"). --short-summary's help text is updated accordingly.
  • SKILL version bumped to 1.1.0 (skills/tmeet-skill/SKILL.md and references/*.md):
    • Command tree redrawn around the new record surface.
    • tmeet-record.md substantially rewritten (~±620-line diff), reorganised around "meeting-domain rules", with form matrices and a common-failure lookup table.
    • tmeet-minutes.md fully rewritten in the global-summary / real-time-summary vocabulary.
  • package.json version bumped to v1.1.0.
  • docs/command.md / docs/command_en.md fully refreshed to reflect the record consolidation and the new update command group.

Removed

  • Eight record subcommand implementation files removed (cmd/record/): list.go, address.go, smart_minutes.go, transcript_get.go, transcript_search.go, transcript_paragraphs.go, permission_apply_prepare.go, permission_apply_commit.go. All of their capabilities are preserved on the new surface via --action; for already-shipped users this is purely a path change with no capability loss.
